hook_frame: There's a ___ detail in this painting most people ___.

lead.credit: The Lute Player-Caravaggio (Metropolitan Museum of Art) — Wikimedia Commons

sentences.text: There's a cruel detail behind this sweet love song that most people never notice.
This is The Lute Player, painted by the Italian master Caravaggio.
Most people see a soft-faced boy singing a madrigal about love.
The open songbook holds love songs set to verses by Petrarch.
And the picture seems to agree.
His lips part and his fingers rest gently on the strings.
A small songbird sits locked inside it.
According to the story of Cardinal del Monte's household, a castrato named Pedro Montoya lived there and sang in the Sistine Chapel.
This rather androgynous model could be him.
Castrati were highly prized at the time.
He isn't a boy singing to a lover.
So is he singing about love, or about the cage he lives in?

meta.title: He Sang Sweet Love Songs... But His Voice Had a Terrible PRICE #history #art
meta.description: The Lute Player by Caravaggio shows a young singer with a songbook of love songs and a caged songbird. The androgynous model could be Pedro Montoya, a castrato of Cardinal del Monte's household who sang in the Sistine Chapel.
meta.question: Is he singing about love, or about his cage?
